messages:
Sophia: Quick drop — pushed an updated battlecard draft into the doc. want fast feedback on the 3 angle tests: cost-first vs reliability-first vs ops-control. link: https://docs.google.com/d/1xExample
Ben: on it. do we have a one-liner per competitor? we should avoid long tables in the slide — sales hates parsing those in 1:1s :grimacing:
Anya: I captured competitor one-liners in the doc under 'rep lines'. short note: cloud AI platforms = "easy access, variable economics"; LLM APIs = "broad model access, w/o infra guarantees"; infra vendors = "you run it, we optimize runtime". feedback welcome.
Mike: For webinars: can we split the narrative? first half demo Redwood runtime savings + live cost calc, second half customer panel on rollback/fallback. CTA: request dedicated consult or trial credits.
Claudia: Routing ask — inbound from webinar should map to a 'launch' lifecycle: product-marketing > SE > AE depending on ARR signal. small leads (<$50k) go to self-serve nurture. big leads flagged to SDR + Solutions Eng. Can we capture this in the battlecard playbook?
Sophia: @Claudia yes, put the routing flow in the battlecard appendix. I'll add an example playbook row: "webinar attendee -> qualification survey -> if infra requirement or SLA mention -> AE route"
Ben: Messaging tweak suggestion: instead of "cost savings" alone, try "predictable inference economics". implies both cost and reliability.
Anya: +1. also add an objection handler for "we already have GPUs on prem" — quick rebuttal: "You can keep models on-prem while using consistent serving policies and SLO tooling — Redwood unifies runtime ops so engineering teams don't reimplement cost/observability"
Mike: For infra vendors comparison: short punchline — "If you want to build a stack and hire ops staff, they win; if you want predictable SLOs and dev experience, Redwood wins." Keep it non-technical in the battlecard summary.
Claudia: Sales enablement request: can we include 3 canned discovery questions? e.g., 1) "What are your 95th percentile latency targets?" 2) "How predictable is your monthly inference bill?" 3) "Have you done a model-level rollback before?"
Sophia: Adding those now. also adding 'whisper' notes for SEs: if a customer mentions multi-region needs, call out dedicated + auto-fallback region routing as a short win.
Ben: Roleplay snippet idea: SE says "if your SLAs are critical, ask about canary rollouts + fallback to smaller model variants". Helps close reliability objections.
Anya: One more: include a micro-benchmark slide: 3 rows (hosted API, dedicated, private) with median latency, median cost/token, recommended workload. keep numbers rounded. sales can call those out in discovery.
Mike: Webinar logistics: run a dry-run w/ SE + 1 customer two days before. Claudia, can your ops calendar the time?
Claudia: Yep, blocking 90m on Tue. I'll add runbook for demo failover: if GPU pool hiccup, flip to cached replies + continue panel Q&A. note in battlecard as fallback script.
Sophia: This is great. last asks: Ben — can you craft 3 subject lines for the post-webinar nurture? Mike — can you draft the demo script for the first 8 minutes showing cost calc? Anya — finalize objection handlers. Claudia — finalize lead routing doc in appendix. I'll merge everything by EOD Friday.
Ben: Subject lines: 1) "How to make LLM inference predictable (and cheaper)" 2) "When cloud AI slips — building inference you can trust" 3) "Reduce inference surprises: real tradeoffs explained"
Mike: Drafting the 8-min script now. will include a live cost calculator snippet and the canary demo.
Anya: I'll tighten objection handlers and add a short FAQ.
Claudia: Routing doc incoming in 30m. I'll annotate with playbook triggers (ARR, compliance, latency).
LaunchBot: Reminder: added a task for "finalize-battlecard" assigned to Sophia with due: 1765190000
Sophia: thanks team. if no major objections I'll publish the beta battlecard to the enablement repo and kick off a sales office hours slot next week. :rocket:
